Chapter 10: The Ongoing Process—Living a Life by Design.
You know, it’s easy to think that once you’ve landed the right job, found the perfect relationship, or settled into a routine that works, you’re all set—that the hard part is over. But here’s the thing: life isn’t really a problem you solve and move on from. It’s more like an ongoing process—a continuous act of creation and discovery. Designing your life isn’t a single event. It’s a practice. It’s about moving through the world with curiosity, intention, and a willingness to adapt, no matter what comes your way.
Picture someone who spent years searching high and low for their true calling. Eventually, he found a job that felt just right. For a while, everything clicked. He was satisfied. But as time went on, fresh questions crept in. He realized that fulfillment isn’t some finish line you cross—it’s more like a moving target. What brings you joy and meaning today might not be the same tomorrow, and that’s completely normal.
Or take a woman who’d built her entire life around raising her kids. When they left home, she was left wondering, What now? The roles that once defined her had faded away. So, she started trying new things—painting, hiking, even learning a new language. Not every experiment stuck. Some fizzled out, but others sparked real passion. She learned that reinvention is always possible, no matter your age or stage of life.
Most of us are taught to chase certainty and steer clear of discomfort. But you know what? Growth actually happens at the edges—right where you’re brave enough to try, to fail, and to start over. There was a young person who, after a string of setbacks, changed their perspective. Instead of seeing life as a straight path, they saw it as a series of experiments. Not every try brought success, but each one offered something new—a lesson, an insight, a fresh direction.
Living a life by design means you stay open to possibility, even when things seem to be going smoothly. It means you check in with yourself on a regular basis. What matters to you right now? What needs to shift? And if you sense it’s time for a change, you’re willing to adjust your course. It’s about holding your plans with a light touch, trusting that new opportunities will appear—even if you can’t see them yet.
Of course, the process isn’t always easy. There will be times filled with doubt, with loss, and plenty of confusion. But there’ll also be moments of clarity, connection, and real joy. The secret? Keep moving. Stay curious. And remember, the journey itself—that winding, ever-changing path—is just as important as wherever you hope to end up.
